sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Introduction to Forestry & Wildlife

topics.title: Forest Concepts, Ecology, Vegetation Zones, Wildlife, and Plant Identification

subtopics.content: Forest vs agriculture, forest ecosystem functions, West African vegetation zones, wildlife management/reserves, plant morphology and tree identification
subtopics.objective: Understand basic forest concepts and ecosystem functions; compare West African vegetation zones (evergreen, semi-deciduous, savannah, mangroves); evaluate wildlife resources, endangered species, and game reserve management; identify plant morphological features, leaf/stem/root anatomy, and tree species.

topics.title: Estate Reservation, Management, Deforestation, Natural and Artificial Regeneration, Agro-Forestry, and Invasive Species

subtopics.content: Reservation processes, protection measures, causes/effects/control of deforestation, natural vs artificial regeneration, agro-forestry systems, Taungya, and invasive weeds
subtopics.objective: Detail forest estate reservation and protection against bushfires and illegal felling; analyze causes, manifestations, and control measures for deforestation; compare natural and artificial regeneration methods; examine agro-forestry practices (alley cropping, silvo-pastoral) and Taungya systems; identify terrestrial and aquatic invasive alien species.

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Plantation Establishment & Forest Mensuration

topics.title: Plantation Planning, Nursery Management, Planting/Tending, and Forest Mensuration

subtopics.content: Plantation design, nursery practices/tools/pests, land preparation, tending operations, operational costing, mensuration tools, enumeration, and surveys
subtopics.objective: Plan and design forest plantations; manage tree nurseries, cultural practices, tools, and pest/disease control; execute planting and tending operations (weeding, pruning, thinning); perform tree measurements (height, diameter, girth, volume) using instruments like Haga altimeters; execute stock sampling and land survey techniques.

sections.sectionTitle: Section D: Harvesting, Marketing, Forest Industries & Income Ventures

topics.title: Timber and NTFP Harvesting, Forest Product Marketing, Timber Industries, Mushroom Cultivation, and Beekeeping

subtopics.content: Pre-harvesting surveys, log markings, transportation, NTFP gathering, harmful harvesting control, demand/marketing agencies, sawmilling, mushroom cultivation, and apiculture
subtopics.objective: Execute timber harvesting procedures, safety protocols, and log marking interpretations; harvest non-timber forest products (NTFPs) and wildlife sustainably; control harmful harvesting practices; analyze market demand, trade agencies, and timber processing industries; establish forestry enterprises; cultivate commercial mushrooms and manage apiaries for honey production.

topics.title: Institutional Framework, Resource Rights, Stakeholders, Land Tenure, and Forest Laws

subtopics.content: Ministry and Forestry Commission structures, TUC/TUP rights acquisition, stakeholder roles, land tenure systems, land registration, and forest policies/laws
subtopics.objective: Understand roles of forestry government divisions, research, and training institutes; detail procedures for acquiring timber utilization contracts and permits; identify stakeholder roles; evaluate land tenure systems, registration, and forest policies and laws.
